newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters praise Clinton, Herman roles in UPS talks.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters praise Clinton, Herman roles in UPS talks.

text.p: A Teamsters union spokeswoman on Monday praised the role of President Bill Clinton and Labor Secretary Alexis Herman in strike talks with United Parcel Service.
But in an interview on Cable News Network, the spokeswoman, Gaye Williams, repeated the union's statement from early in the day that both sides were still far apart on major issues.
"I think the president and Secretary of Labor Herman have done a good job in keeping the talks going and keeping UPS at the bargaining table," Williams said.
Her comments came one day after Clinton expressed optimism that the two parties were very close to settling their two-week-old dispute.

"It's my gut feeling they'll settle," the president told reporters as he arrived at Martha's Vineyard on Sunday in Massachusetts for a three-week vacation. "They're that close," he said, holding up two fingers not very far apart.
But Williams, speaking to the contrary, told CNN "there has not been agreement on any of the major issues" and did not give any indication the union and UPS were close to ending the strike.
When asked by CNN what the president meant by his remarks, Williams simply said: "I can't speak for the president. I'm not sure what information he has."
She announced that on Thursday the Teamsters union is having a "day of action" and urged people who support the union's position in the strike to wear blue ribbons.
